summary: The bots trained for 3 rounds: 14400 air-only matches, 2 against 2, 6 game-minutes each. A change was kept only when it won by more than luck.

Bf 109 G-6: kept its tactics: nothing tried beat the noise. Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 0.2 before, 0.2 after; own crashes and collisions 0.09 per life before, 0.09 after.

Spitfire Mk IX: learned to change firing range (1 → 1.15). Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, opens fire at 115% of the usual range, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 0.72 before, 0.83 after; own crashes and collisions 0.1 per life before, 0.1 after.

P-47D Thunderbolt: learned to change firing range (1 → 1.15). Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, opens fire at 115% of the usual range, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 0.26 before, 0.34 after; own crashes and collisions 0.1 per life before, 0.12 after.

La-5FN: kept its tactics: nothing tried beat the noise. Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 0.37 before, 0.36 after; own crashes and collisions 0.15 per life before, 0.14 after.

Ki-43-II Hayabusa: kept its tactics: nothing tried beat the noise. Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 0.15 before, 0.14 after; own crashes and collisions 0.1 per life before, 0.09 after.

Brewster B-239: learned to change firing range (1 → 1.15). Now it turn-fights, never breaks off, opens fire at 115% of the usual range, throttles back in turns. Kills per life 1.09 before, 1.11 after; own crashes and collisions 0.16 per life before, 0.12 after.
The kills-per-life numbers are from a short check (every pairing, a few matches), so small changes there can be luck. The Balance Lab run started next shows the effect on the real battle.
